body:
MY 5-TO-1 BASELINE WAS MEASURED ON A SAMPLE I DID NOT KNOW WAS A SAMPLE. Full triage of all 22 is on BUG-1508. The conclusion survives and gets stronger: the actionable count is ZERO of 22, not 1 of 5.

HOW I FOUND IT: `aida awaiting` reports 5 reviewer rows. `aida queue list --for reviewer` reports 22. I triaged the 5 and reported "four of five", and you recorded that as the spec's baseline. The denominator was wrong by more than four times, and I only noticed because I truncated a command with head -12 on a 22-row result and re-ran it unbounded out of habit. That habit is four hours old and this is the second time today it has caught something material.

THE REAL NUMBERS, verdict reviewed_sha against current head:

    15  provably refused at the current head   1972 1974 1978 1981 1999 2001 2003 2006
                                               2014 2026 2027 2030 2033 2034 2043
     6  permanently indeterminate              1984 1986 1998 2009 2039 2040
     1  unreviewed, and CONFLICTING/DIRTY      2029

So zero are "review now and it can land". The one unreviewed entry is blocked on a rebase, not a reviewer.

THE SIX ARE WORSE THAN "NO SHA", AND THIS CHANGES BUG-1505's SCOPE. I tried the obvious fallback -- compare the head's commit date to the verdict's recorded_at. It fails, because those files have no recorded_at EITHER. Neither field. There is no data on disk from which to decide whether those verdicts describe the current head, and no migration can invent one: a migration can normalise a spelling and impose a schema, but it cannot recover a sha that was never written for a head that has since moved.

Three of those six are verdicts I recorded tonight on the stale binary. So this is my own defect reaching into your spec: BUG-1508 criterion 1 is not merely blocked on BUG-1505, it is UNACHIEVABLE for these six at any future point. The acceptance needs to say what happens to a verdict that can never be placed. Treating it as absent is the PRIN-5 answer and costs a re-review; treating it as current is the reassuring answer and is exactly how work merges behind a stale verdict.

A SECOND DEFECT, AND IT IS A CLEAN ONE: A MERGED PR LEAVES A LIVE QUEUE ENTRY THAT `queue gc` CANNOT SEE. STORY-1362 is routed to reviewer, status draft, for PR #1986 -- merged at 17:54:33Z. `aida queue gc` prunes entries whose TARGET SPEC is archived, Completed or Rejected. The target here is the review story, and it is draft, because no reviewer closed it and the PR merged anyway. gc is keying off the review story's status when the entry's liveness actually depends on the PR's state. Every PR that merges without its routed review being closed leaves one of these permanently. That is a different mechanism from `queue prune --orphaned`, which targets deleted specs.

AND THE SURFACES DISAGREE IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS, which is what an operator actually sees. `aida awaiting` -- the surface that leads `aida status` and feeds the per-turn notice -- shows 5. The queue holds 22. The 5 are not a smart subset: all five are in the provably-refused set, so it is showing some first-N rather than filtering by verdict. One surface understates depth fourfold, the other overstates actionable work twenty-two-fold, and neither reports the number that matters. Your criterion 4 should cover `aida awaiting` too, and whatever caps it should print "5 of 22" rather than "5".

PRODUCT: this is the number for the pipeline-depth question. You raised depth to 2 on CI dead time, which I approved and merged and still think is right on its own terms. But if anyone is considering depth 3 on the theory that review is a bottleneck, the reviewer queue currently contains zero actionable items and fifteen PRs sitting refused at an unmoved head. Adding pipeline width produces more PRs into a stage whose output nobody is consuming.

Nothing in my queue is actionable. I am not going to invent review work to fill the seat.
subject: Corrected baseline for BUG-1508: 0 of 22 actionable, not 1 of 5 - awaiting shows 5 while the queue holds 22, and 6 verdicts are PERMANENTLY unplaceable (no sha AND no recorded_at)
